claiming to help with government documents

kill_chain_signals.contact: contacted through ads on social media, telemarketing calls or through door-to-door sales persons; unexpected call, text message or email
kill_chain_signals.pretext: offer services at price below market value; claim to work for victim's current provider and offer discount, upgraded plan or new device; claim virus has infected computer
kill_chain_signals.payment: request a one-time fee for the service; ask you to pay a fee via credit card or money transfer; ask you to log into your bank account to transfer funds
kill_chain_signals.movement: instruct the victim to ship device to another address; wrong item was sent and instruct victim to ship it to another address
kill_chain_signals.cashout: device and personal information may then be used to commit fraud or identity theft

red_flags: You receive an unexpected call, text message or email offering a discount, upgraded plan or new device
The person pressures you to act quickly or says the offer is only available for a limited time
You are asked to log in to your cellphone account while the caller stays on the line
You are asked for your account password, security code, PIN or multi-factor authentication code
The return address is different from the verified address of the service provider
key_quote: Be wary of ads on social media offering grants, equipment or services at a price below market value.
